slides.title: It starts with your phone.
slides.text: Your phone is a {device}: an {identity} of its own, something that can act. Inside it sits a {signer}: a {key}, a secret only the phone holds, that can say one thing: “this really comes from this phone.” A signer is not an identity; it is just the device's current key.
slides.deep: A device identity's ID is the hash of its birth record, which its first signer signs itself, so the ID outlives every key. How the key is kept is up to the device: on a phone, derived from the passkey's PRF plus a per-device salt; on a laptop, the keychain; on a server, an environment variable, a secret manager or an HSM.

slides.title: Your devices act for you.
slides.text: You are an identity too: a {human}. Your phone, laptop and watch are {members} of you: they act for you, each with its own signer. A device is a member of exactly one identity: you, or, for a shared server, a coop, which you'll meet next. Lose a device, add another, and you're still you.
slides.deep: One kind of link only, always pointing up: signer (a key) → device → human → coop. Authority flows up (the device signs, so you act); control flows down (you add and remove your devices by your own rules). Identity types: device, human, coop.

slides.title: How it all starts.
slides.text: First comes your first device: it makes its signer and signs its own birth. Then you are born: your birth is signed by that device, names it as your first member, and already names your next keys. Every later device joins from both sides: it signs “I act for you”, and you sign “this device is mine”. Only both together count.
flow: you are born, signed by it
each new device: both sides sign
slides.deep: No loop: the device's birth needs no one; the human's birth needs one device; every later membership needs two signatures, the device's and the human's under its own rules. Nobody can claim someone else's device, and no device can attach itself to someone else.

slides.title: You and Mia start a home.
slides.text: Together you form a {coop}: an identity made of identities. Neither of you is the coop alone, and it lives on even if one of you loses every device.
slides.deep: A coop's members are identities, never signers, and membership may not form a cycle.

slides.title: Coops can hold coops.
slides.text: Your street is a coop of homes, and a home is a coop of people. Coops can be members of coops, as deep as you like, just never in a circle.
slides.deep: Identity types: device, human, coop. A coop's members are human or coop identities; a human's members are device identities. Cycles are rejected when a membership change is checked.

slides.title: A coop decides by its own signing rules.
slides.text: A coop has members, and its own {signing rules}: who must agree for the coop to act. They know only three kinds of act. Acting: ordinary changes. Owning: writing the rules for data it owns, and handing data over (Data chapter). Governing: changing its own members and signing rules. Signing rules never mention a piece of data.
slides.deep: Same shape as every rule in theOS: who (its members), on what (the coop itself), operations (act, own, govern), conditions (threshold, weights, all-of / any-of, time locks). Conditions are plugins; a device that does not know one treats it as not satisfied.

slides.title: Losing your phone.
slides.text: Every identity keeps a signed {history} of its keys and members. When it was born, that history named its next keys, so you can switch to them. You mark the lost phone as gone, and from then on it can sign nothing for you. What it could still read comes in the Keys chapter.
slides.deep: Pre-rotation (KERI): the birth record commits to the hash of the next keys. The device identity of the lost phone is removed from the human identity's members, so its signer no longer counts.

slides.title: Identity, in short.
list: A device is an identity of its own; its signer is only a key.
A human identity's members are its devices.
A coop is an identity made of identities, and coops can hold coops.
Each identity decides by its own signing rules: act, own, govern.
slides.deep: Three identity types: device, human, coop. Every identity's ID is the hash of its birth record, so it outlives all of its keys.
